:::note[About this page]
This page is an unofficial guide to S1000D® Issue 7, written in this project's own words. It is based on the S1000D distribution dated 2026-07-16. This is a personal project and is not affiliated with ASD ([Specification files and trademarks](/s1000d-stack/guide/license/)). The formal definition is in Chap 3.9.5.1 of the S1000D specification and in the [S1000D Issue 7 data dictionary](https://users.s1000d.org/S1000D_DD_7/Files/attributes/issueNumber.xml).
:::

`issueNumber` is the attribute that gives the issue number of a data module or a data management list. Together with [`inWork`](/s1000d-stack/reference/s1000d/issue-7/in-work/), it identifies an issue.

## Elements that carry it

In the 33 XML schemas of Issue 7, 2 elements carry this attribute.

| Element | Schemas | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issueInfo` | 28 | Required |
| `targetDmIssueInfo` | 1 | Required |

## Allowed values

The allowed values are decided by the XML schema. The default BREX (Business Rules Exchange) has no rule that lists the values of this attribute.

| Defined by | Content |
| --- | --- |
| XML schema | The type is `issueNumberAttType` (based on `xs:nonNegativeInteger`). The pattern is `\d{3,5}` |

## Related rules

- Up to the first release, in-work issues are `000` and the first release is `001` (BREX-S1-00030 of the default BREX).
- A value below 1,000 is written with three digits (BREX-S1-00274). A value from 1,000 to 9,999 is written with four digits (BREX-S1-00275).
- In a file name, the issue number and the in-work number are written like `_002-01`.

## In this stack

| Operation | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Read | [`list_data_modules`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/list-data-modules/) and [`read_data_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/read-data-module/). The value is in `issueInfo` |
| Decide it when a data module is created | [`build_data_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/build-data-module/). Pass `issueInfo` in the draft, or let `issuePolicy` (`increment-issue`, `increment-inwork`, `keep`) decide |
| Start an in-work issue | [`start_revision`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/start-revision/). It does not change `issueNumber` |

This stack does not yet have an operation that releases an issue (setting `inWork` back to `00` and raising `issueNumber`).
